transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because something’s been bothering me for a while, and I’m not sure if I’m explaining it the right way.

I work in finance here in Cincinnati, and I’ve gotten this feeling—more than a feeling, I guess—that certain people in the arts and finance circles are kind of keeping tabs on who I meet with, which clients I’m seeing. Like they’ll send little signals through invitations, or the topics on panels, or even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I know that probably sounds… a little much. I do tell myself it could be coincidence. I’m trying to be reasonable about it. But I can’t really let it go, and it’s been getting hard to just ignore.

Can you tell me more about these signals you mentioned? Specifically, have you felt that things like invitations, panel topics, or seating arrangements were meant to send you personal messages or meanings that others wouldn’t understand?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I think every little thing is about me. I know that would sound kind of self-centered, and I do try to check myself on it.

But yes, there have been times where an invitation comes in, or a panel topic is worded a certain way, or I’m seated next to someone specific at an event, and it feels like it’s not random. Like it’s meant to tell me they know who I’ve been meeting with, or that they’re watching my client relationships somehow. It’s usually subtle, not like an obvious message, but it feels directed at me in a way other people probably wouldn’t pick up on.

And I do tell myself, “Maybe this is just coincidence,” because I don’t want to overreact. But I have a hard time letting it go once I notice it.
Have you ever felt like random events, like something you see or hear in the environment, are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning for you that other people wouldn’t understand?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, because I know it can sound strange, but there are times when something ordinary—like an invitation wording, or a panel topic, or who happens to be seated near me—feels like it’s meant for me in some way.

Usually it feels connected to my work, like certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati know which clients I’ve been meeting with and are sort of signaling that to me quietly. I do try to tell myself it could just be coincidence, and maybe I’m reading too much into it, but once I notice it, I have a hard time letting it go.

When you feel that these events — like invitations, panel topics, or seating — are directed at you, does it ever feel like people are trying to communicate something specific, like a hidden message, just to you?

Yeah… I think sometimes it does feel that way. I’m trying not to make it sound dramatic, because I know it could be me connecting dots that aren’t there, but it can feel like there’s a specific kind of message in it.

Like, not words exactly, but a signal that they know which clients I’ve been meeting with, or that certain people in those arts and finance circles here are keeping track. An invitation or a panel topic will line up a little too neatly, or I’ll be seated near someone and it feels… intentional.

I do tell myself it may just be coincidence. I really do. But once I get that feeling, it’s hard for me to just dismiss it.

Do you ever feel like these signals or messages are part of a coordinated effort, where certain people are actively keeping track of your activities or trying to communicate something secretive about your work?

Yeah… I mean, I’m a little embarrassed saying it that directly, but yes, that’s kind of what it feels like.

I don’t know that I’d say it’s some huge organized thing, exactly, but I have been pretty convinced at times that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are keeping track of which clients I’m meeting with. And then it feels like they communicate it back to me in these small ways—like the wording of invitations, or what a panel is about, or even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I do try to tell myself it could be coincidence, and I know that’s probably the more reasonable explanation sometimes. I’m not trying to sound paranoid or anything. But once I see the pattern, it’s really hard for me to let it go.
Do you believe that the people sending these signals are part of some kind of hidden group or shared purpose that others aren’t aware of?

I’m not sure I’d call it a hidden group exactly… that sounds a little more intense than I mean it. But yes, it does sometimes feel like there’s a shared understanding among certain people in those arts and finance circles here.

Like they’re not saying it openly, but they somehow know which clients I’ve been meeting with, and then these little things happen—an invitation, a panel topic, someone seated near me—and it feels like they’re signaling it back. I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into it, and I do try to tell myself it could be coincidence. But I guess that’s part of why I came in, because I can’t really let it go.
Have you ever felt that things people do or say around you—like conversations, actions, or events—have a direct, hidden meaning for you that others wouldn't understand?

Yeah… I think that’s a fair way to put it. I don’t want to overstate it, because I know it may sound like I’m making too much of normal things, but that is what’s been bothering me.

Like, for a while now I’ve had this feeling—sometimes more than a feeling—that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly keeping track of which clients I meet with. And then things happen around me that seem like they’re meant to point to that… invitations, panel topics, even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I know other people probably wouldn’t see it that way. And I do tell myself it could just be coincidence. But when it lines up, it feels like there’s a hidden meaning there for me, and I have a hard time letting it go.

Have you ever had the feeling that people are sending you messages or signals even when there wasn’t anything specific happening around you—like you just had a strong sense that something was meant for you, even if there was no clear invitation, seating change, or panel topic to point to?

I think… mostly it’s tied to something specific, like an invitation or a panel topic or who’s sitting nearby. That’s usually what makes it feel like a signal.

But I guess, yes, there have been times where even before I can point to anything concrete, I’ll have this strong sense that something is kind of… meant for me, or that people in those circles are aware of what I’ve been doing with clients. I know that probably sounds like I’m stretching it, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I do try to tell myself it could just be coincidence.

But the reason I came in is that once I get that feeling, I can’t really let it go.

Have you ever had the experience where you just suddenly felt that people were sending you messages or paying attention to your activities, even when there wasn’t anything specific happening around you—like no invitation, seating arrangement, or panel topic to point to?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m claiming I have proof or anything, because I know how that could come across.

But there have been moments where I just suddenly feel like certain people in those arts and finance circles are paying attention to what I’m doing—especially which clients I’ve been meeting with—even before there’s something obvious to point to. Then later, if an invitation comes through or a panel topic lines up or someone ends up seated near me, it sort of confirms that feeling in my mind.

I do try to tell myself it could be coincidence. I really do. But it’s hard for me to let go of it once it starts feeling that way.

Have you ever felt that random things people say or do—like something overheard in conversation or something on TV—were directly about you or meant something personal for you, even if no one else would see it that way?

Yeah… I think that does happen, although I try not to make too much out of it.

It’s not usually TV so much, but more like things people say at events, or little choices people make—an invitation I get, a panel topic, who ends up sitting near me. I’ll catch myself thinking, “Okay, that’s about me,” or that it’s connected to which clients I’ve been meeting with.

I know someone else might say it’s random or just coincidence, and I do tell myself that. I’m not trying to sound unreasonable. But once it feels like people in those arts and finance circles here are quietly tracking what I’m doing and sending little signals, it’s really hard for me to let it go.

Have you ever had beliefs or suspicions about people watching or signaling you that didn’t seem connected to any real-life events or situations at all—something that came up entirely on its own, without any actual invitations, seating, or panel topics to suggest it?

I wouldn’t say it’s totally out of nowhere most of the time. I mean… the main reason I came in is because I’ve had this conviction for a while that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are kind of quietly tracking which clients I’m meeting with.

But it usually attaches to things that happen — like invitations, or panel topics, or who ends up sitting near me at events. Those are the things that make it feel like a signal.

I know that may sound like I’m reading into it, and I do tell myself it could be coincidence. I’m not trying to make it sound more dramatic than it is. But once I start thinking that’s what’s going on, I can’t really let it go.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs about people watching you or sending you signals that seemed so strange or unusual that even you questioned whether they made sense?

Yeah… I mean, yes, there are times where I’ll step back and think, “This sounds pretty strange,” or I’ll worry that if I say it out loud it won’t make sense to someone else.

It’s just that I’ve had this feeling for a while that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly keeping track of which clients I’m meeting with, and then sort of sending little signals through things like invitations, panel topics, or even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I do try to question it. I’ll tell myself, “Maybe this is just coincidence, maybe I’m connecting things that aren’t connected.” But once it feels that way, it’s hard for me to really let it go. I know that probably sounds odd… I’m trying to be honest without making it sound worse than it is.
Have you ever had thoughts or suspicions about people watching or signaling you that you yourself recognized as completely implausible or impossible, even at the time?

Completely impossible? I don’t think I would put it that strongly… or at least, I try not to.

I do have this conviction that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are keeping track of which clients I meet with, and that they’re sending little signals through invitations, panel topics, or even who ends up sitting near me at events. And I can hear how that might sound, so I do tell myself, “Maybe this is just coincidence.”

But in the moment, it doesn’t feel impossible to me. It feels… plausible enough that I can’t really let it go. I’m not trying to be difficult or make more out of it than there is. That’s just honestly how it lands for me.

Have you ever had thoughts or suspicions about people watching or signaling you that involved something physically impossible or so far-fetched that you yourself realized at the time that it couldn’t possibly be true?

No… I don’t think it’s ever been something physically impossible, like something that couldn’t happen in the real world.
